newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, awaits LME stock data.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, awaits LME stock data.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly weaker following a quiet and rangebound session as traders waited for Friday's LME stock report.
The market largely agreed that stocks will rise, but were unsure by how much with estimates ranging from a modest 2,000 tonnes to a sharp hike of 10,000 tonnes.
David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said the strong backwardation on LME was bound to draw some material into warehouses.

"But the market should hold above a dollar per pound because of the very tight supply nearby and the prospects that we won't see this anticipated shift to a surplus until the second quarter of next year," Rinehimer said.
Many analysts had forecast a surplus in the copper market by the end of this year but LME stocks have plunged to six-year lows.
March COMEX settled 0.60 cent lower at 101.15 cents a lb, traded 102.30 to 100.10 cents. Spot December went out 0.40 cent weaker at 104.85 cents.
Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots with 1,003 switches, compared to Wednesday's official volume of 9,999 lots.
The cash to three months backwardation on the LME eased on Thursday to $150/$154.
